text:
maria: Heads-up — multiple customers reported short 3–6s spikes from bulk-import jobs hitting per-key quotas and getting throttled. Steady-state looks fine. Thinking we should add a short ‘grace’ window at the rate limiter to absorb micro spikes. Anyone see pitfalls?

sam: Yep, makes sense. My mental model: allow a small forgiveness budget that can be consumed for N ms before enforcement kicks in. Prefer an additive small credit bucket that decays instead of just delaying enforcement.

li: This would live in the rate-limiter layer, right? Not the routing layer. We already have caching upstream, but this is about smoothing enforcement to reduce noisy alerts. If we add this, we must track metrics: rl.forgive_applied, rl.forgive_count, rl.forgive_latency_ms so we can audit and alert.

alex: Example config sketch to discuss (pseudo-yaml):
```
rate_limit:
  capacity: 200
  refill_per_sec: 100
forgiveness_policy:
  mode: "budget"   # budget | delay
  window_ms: 600     # how long a forgiveness event can last
  max_budget_tokens: 75  # total short-term tokens available
  budget_refill_per_min: 5
```
This gives short bursts some breathing room but recharges slowly so it isn't a permanent bypass.

infra-bot: test-run: rl-bench v2 shows 4.3% fewer throttles at p99 for short spike traces with a 600ms window on a synthetic 10k-import trace. Details: ci/rl/bench/1818034567.

sam: Rollout plan idea: feature flag rl_forgive_v1 (default off). Canary 1% orgs for 24h, measure: overall tokens consumed, forgiven vs enforced, request latency, and error surface. If no regressions, expand to 25% then 100% over a week. Add rollback if rl.enforced_errors increase > 0.5% over baseline.

maria: Fairness concern — large orgs with frequent imports could repeatedly consume forgiveness budget and starve small orgs. We should scope forgiveness per (org,key) and have a per-org daily cap + decay. Also show budget usage in console so customers understand behavior.

li: Implementation details: store forgiveness_budget in redis keyed by org:key with TTL; budget decays via refill rate, and we emit events when budget drops below thresholds. Also add a hard cap that prevents enforcement being fully disabled. E.g., max_forgive_tokens_per_minute = min(global_limit, org_quota * 0.05).

alex: Console UX: new tile on Quotas page "Burst forgiveness" with toggle + explainer, histogram of forgiven spikes, and a timeseries of forgiven_tokens vs enforcement_count. Also a quick links area: "request higher steady quota" and "view recent forgiven traces". For rollouts expose an override per-org so support can test.

sam: Tests: unit tests around budget decrement and refill logic, e2e with synthetic import traces, and a canary job that runs against a snapshot of production traffic. I'll prototype in rate-limiter repo and open a draft PR.

maria: Sounds good. Action items: sam to prototype PR + bench (ETA Tue), li to spec telemetry events and redis key schemas (ETA Tue), alex to mock console tile and copy for UX (ETA Wed). I'll draft rollout playbook and SLA notes. :thumbsup:

alex: +1. If someone can pair on the bench I'll join tomorrow morning.

li: ack, will pair for 30m at 10:00.

maria: thanks everyone — keeping this small and observable seems key. We can iterate on parameters after canary.

sam: SG, will post PR link here when ready.
